answersOpenItem: BT836's second Open bullet: whether the 11-cell's gluing is the Paley/biplane structure on 11. It is.

coxeter.source: H.S.M. Coxeter, 'A Symmetrical Arrangement of Eleven Hemi-Icosahedra', Ann. Discrete Math. 20 (1984); polytope due to Grunbaum 1976/77
coxeter.construction: cyclically permute GF(11) and take the hexad 02678t; any two of the 11 share a triangle, and each hexad's 10 triangles form the hemi-icosahedron {3,5}_5

arithmeticReading.why: the 11 hexads are complements of the 11 translates of the residue set, and those translates are the blocks of the Paley biplane

correctionToPreviousCommit: gc_connection_is_cell_level_only.py presented the non-embedding of PSL(2,11) and PSL(2,19) in Sp(4,3) as its own boundary. BT836 already states it in its Physics/machine reading. That file's actual contribution is the one-line divisibility proof and the count mismatch, not the boundary itself.
boundary: this is about the 11-cell's internal structure. It does NOT place PSL(2,11) inside Sp(4,3), which remains impossible, and it does not connect the biplane to W(3,3). BT836's Singer Z_13 / Z_7 clock half is untouched.
